title: The Transformer as a Polar State Estimator
abstract: arXiv:2605.11007v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We show that the core components of the Transformer---attention, residual connections, and normalization---arise naturally from a single geometric state estimation problem. Modeling the latent state in polar coordinates naturally separates radial and hyperspherical dynamics, yielding a precision-weighted filtering procedure in which normalization enforces the hyperspherical constraint, attention aggregates directional evidence, and the residual connection implements an incremental state update. The standard Transformer block with rotary positional encodings is recovered by discarding the geometric correction terms of the resulting state estimator, showing that its architecture follows from the underlying estimation problem rather than from independent design choices. The proposed \textit{Polar Transformer} retains these geometric corrections.

translated_title: 作为极坐标状态估计器的Transformer
translated_abstract: 我们证明，Transformer的核心组件——注意力机制、残差连接和归一化——自然地源于一个单一的几何状态估计问题。在极坐标下对潜在状态进行建模，可以自然地将径向动力学与超球面动力学分离开来，从而产生一种精度加权滤波程序：其中归一化强制执行超球面约束，注意力机制聚合方向证据，残差连接实现增量式状态更新。通过舍弃所得状态估计器中的几何修正项，即可恢复出带有旋转位置编码的标准Transformer块，这表明其架构源自底层的估计问题，而非独立的设计选择。本文提出的“极坐标Transformer”（Polar Transformer）保留了这些几何修正项。
tldr: 本文证明Transformer的注意力机制、残差连接和归一化组件可从极坐标下的几何状态估计问题中自然推导得出，并提出保留了这些几何修正项的Polar Transformer。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that the Transformer's core components—attention, residual connections, and normalization—naturally arise from a geometric state estimation problem in polar coordinates, and proposes the Polar Transformer that retains the geometric correction terms.
